comment.body: Good catch, this is real. In Vue 3.2.47, static text keeps its surrounding whitespace (condensed to a single space), but whitespace next to an interpolation is dropped. So the link text gained spaces: ` guide on recording runs ` instead of `guide on recording runs`, and ` Learn more ` instead of `Learn more `. Fixed in c9a1600 by interpolating the literals (`{{ 'guide on recording runs' }}` etc.) in `DebugTour.vue` and `DebugEmptyView.vue`, plus a short comment on why. Writing the text on one line against the tags isn't an option, because `vue/singleline-html-element-content-newline` and `vue/html-indent` reject it. I rendered both the old and new templates with Vue's SSR renderer, and the output now matches the i18n version byte-for-byte: - `Review the guide on recording runs to Cypress Cloud` - `Learn more …` The three debug empty-state specs still pass (10/10), along with `check-ts`, `lint` and `health-check`. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

issue.title: chore: inline plain strings in app debug page components (part 1)
issue.body:
- Closes N/A — part of the internal effort to remove vue-i18n from the Vue frontends (batch A1). This is a mechanical refactor with no behavior change.

### Additional details

The app only ships English, so this batch swaps vue-i18n lookups for the plain English strings from `en-US.json` in the first set of debug page components. The tests now assert on literal strings too.

**Components converted** (`packages/app/src/debug/`):
- `DebugCancelledAlert.vue`
- `DebugContainer.vue`
- `DebugErrored.vue`
- `DebugNoTests.vue`
- `DebugOverLimit.vue`
- `DebugPageHeader.vue`
- `DebugPassed.vue`
- `DebugPendingRunCounts.vue`
- `DebugPendingRunSplash.vue`

**Specs updated:** `DebugContainer.cy.tsx` and `DebugPageHeader.cy.tsx` now use literal strings in place of `defaultMessages`.

A few details worth a closer look:
- **Plurals:** these became plain conditionals that match vue-i18n's default rules. When a message gets a named `n`, vue-i18n picks the plural form from `n`. That means "spec skipped / specs skipped" follows `totalSpecs`, not the number of skipped specs.
- **Commits ahead:** `DebugPageHeader` builds this text in a small `commitsAheadText` computed. When I wrote the same ternary straight into the template, the component spec crashed every time with `read ECONNRESET` in the test runner, even though the text it rendered was identical. The computed version passes every time. I couldn't pin down why, so it may be worth watching on CI.
- **Null retention days:** `dataRetentionDays` is nullable in the schema. vue-i18n showed `null` as an empty string, so the message falls back to `''` to keep the text the same.
- **`DebugFailedTest.vue` keeps `useI18n` for now:** its only use of `t` is passing it to `getDebugArtifacts()` in `utils/debugArtifacts.ts`, which is outside this batch. `GroupedDebugFailedTest.vue` calls the helper the same way. The batch that covers that helper can remove all three together.

`en-US.json`, `i18n.ts`, the support files and `package.json` are deliberately left alone. Other batches run in parallel, and a final task removes them.

### Steps to test

Run the component specs that cover these components:

```bash
env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE yarn workspace @packages/app cypress:run:ct --browser electron --spec "src/debug/DebugContainer.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugPageHeader.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugPendingRunCounts.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugPendingRunSplash.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugFailedTest.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugRunStates.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugRunNavigation.cy.tsx,src/debug/DebugTestingProgress.cy.tsx"
```

I ran each spec on its own, before and after the change, and the results matched:

| Spec | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `DebugContainer` | 26/26 | 26/26 |
| `DebugPageHeader` | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| `DebugPendingRunCounts` | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| `DebugPendingRunSplash` | 2/2 | 2/2 |
| `DebugFailedTest` | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| `DebugRunStates` | 12/12 | 12/12 |

`DebugRunNavigation` (11/11) and `DebugTestingProgress` (2/2) pass after the change; I didn't run them before it. `yarn check-ts --scope @packages/app`, `yarn lint --scope @packages/app` and `yarn health-check` all pass.

`cypress/e2e/debug.cy.ts` also asserts some of these strings, but I couldn't run it locally because Cypress-in-Cypress e2e needs a real Chrome install. CI will cover it.

### How has the user experience changed?

No change. The text on screen is byte-for-byte the same.

### PR Tasks

- [na] Is there an associated issue with maintainer approval for PR submission? Internal refactor; see the description.
- [x] Have tests been added/updated?
- [na] Has a PR for user-facing changes been opened in [`cypress-documentation`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation)?
- [na] Have API changes been updated in the [`type definitions`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/types/cypress.d.ts)?

> Mechanical string swap with matching component tests; no auth, data, or API changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Part one of removing **vue-i18n** from the app debug UI: nine components under `packages/app/src/debug/` now render **hard-coded English** that matches the previous `en-US` copy, with **`useI18n` / `t()` removed** from each.
>

issue.title: chore: adopt eslint-plugin-n for Node runtime floors and dependencies
issue.body:
- Closes N/A. This is one slice of adopting lint plugins that enforce rules the repo already documents but checks by hand (the runtime floors in AGENTS.md "Runtime targets").

### Additional details

Adds `nodeConfig` to `@packages/eslint-config`, built on `eslint-plugin-n` ^18.5, and opts every Node-side workspace into it. It enables:

- `n/no-unsupported-features/node-builtins`, `es-builtins` and `es-syntax`
- `n/no-extraneous-import` and `n/no-extraneous-require`

**Floors.** The floors are set explicitly rather than read from `engines`, which most workspaces don't declare. Both are read at load time from the files that own them, so they can't drift:

- **Default floor:** `>=` the `.node-version` version (24.22.1). That's also the Node embedded in the pinned Electron 43.8.4, so the main process has the same floor.
- **User floor:** `userNodeConfig` lowers it to `engines.node` from `cli/package.json` (`^22.0.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0`). It applies to:
  - the shipped CLI, but not `cli/test/**`, whose specs CI runs on the dev Node
  - `packages/server/lib/plugins/child/**`, the config child process

**Opt-ins.** Every workspace opts in except the browser bundles (`app`, `launchpad`, `frontend-shared`, `driver`, `reporter`, `runner`, `extension`, `example`) and the `npm/` mount adapters. Some opted-in packages also ship browser code, and those files are left out too:

- `vite-dev-server`'s and `vite-plugin-cypress-esm`'s `client/**`
- `webpack-dev-server`'s `src/browser.ts` and `src/aut-runner.ts`

`system-tests` leaves out `projects/**` and `project-fixtures/**`, where `no-extraneous-import` crashes resolving the fixtures' tsconfig files.

**Two things the initial probe missed:**

- **Undeclared deps hidden by an unbuilt tree.** `no-extraneous-*` skips imports it can't resolve, and workspaces whose `main` points at build output don't resolve until built. Linting a built tree, as CI does, turned up 17 more hits beyond the probe's 40.
- **Node globals.** The plugin only checks globals such as `process` and `Buffer` that resolve in scope. Workspaces that never declared Node globals (`cli`, for one) were silently skipping those checks, so `nodeConfig` now declares `globals.node`.

**What the rules reported, and the fixes:**

- **Undeclared sibling workspaces:** declared as `0.0.0-development` `devDependencies`, as the repo already does, unless the declaration would close a dependency cycle. nx breaks a cycle by dropping one of its edges, which can build a package before one it compiles against. Declaring `@packages/https-proxy` in `network` did exactly that in CI (`https-proxy` built before `network`). Ten imports would close a cycle, so they aren't declared. The importing files get `undeclaredWorkspaceImports(files, workspaces)` instead, a new export that sets `allowModules` for just those files. No edge this PR adds closes a cycle.
- **Undeclared packages in `scripts`:** declared in its `dependencies`, reusing ranges already in the lockfile so nothing resolves a new copy.
- **Type-only imports:** declared `@angular-devkit/core` in `webpack-dev-server` and `@types/request` in `@packages/ts`.
- **Intentional cross-package resolution:** `eslint-disable-next-line` with a reason for `playwright-core` (found through `playwright-webkit`), `html-webpack-plugin` (found in the user's project) and the batteries-included preprocessor (found in the Cypress binary).
- **The 5 `node-builtins` hits:** 4 were the browser's `Storage` type in `cli/types/cypress.d.ts`, and 1 was `zlib.crc32` in a CLI spec that runs on the dev Node. The version rules are now off for `.d.ts` files, which emit no code.

**Notes:**

- The plugin is loaded with `require`: its types use a string-named export (`"module.exports"`) that TypeScript only parses from 5.6, and the repo is on 5.4.5.
- `n/no-process-exit` stays off, because its hits are CLIs and scripts that exit on purpose. `n/no-deprecated-api` is left for a separate slice.
- `yarn dedupe-lockfile` bumped `ignore`, `get-tsconfig` and `@eslint-community/regexpp` within their existing ranges.

`packages/eslint-config/AGENTS.md` documents the block: what it checks, the floors, which workspaces opt in and why the rest don't, the cycle rule, and the gotchas above.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Lint and dependency-declaration only; no runtime behavior changes beyond ESLint enforcement in CI and local dev.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`nodeConfig`** to `@packages/eslint-config` on **`eslint-plugin-n`**, enforcing Node/ES feature floors and **`n/no-extraneous-import` / `require`** across Node-side workspaces. Floors come from **`.node-version`** (bundled/dev) and **`cli/package.json` `engines.node`** via **`userNodeConfig`** for shipped CLI code and **`packages/server/lib/plugins/child/**`**.
> 
> Opt-in is wired through dozens of **`eslint.config.ts`** files, with **ignores** for browser bundles, webpack/vite client code, and **system-tests** fixtures. **`undeclaredWorkspaceImports`** whitelists sibling workspace imports that would create **nx build cycles** if declared in **`package.json`**.
> 
> Dependency and **`package.json`** updates (plus a few targeted **`eslint-disable`** comments) fix new extraneous-import hits; **`AGENTS.md`** documents adoption, floors, and gotchas (built tree for resolution, **`globals.node`**, **`require`** for the plugin).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 41d467d934f3d432f9514d5d2309ab18edc8a20b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

### Steps to test

1. Run `yarn build`, then `yarn lint`. It should pass. Run it on a built tree, or the dependency rules can't see workspaces whose `main` points at build output.
2. To confirm the floors fire, add `export const fs = process.getBuiltinModule('fs')` (added in Node 22.3) to a file in each place below, then run `npx eslint <file>` from that workspace:
   - `cli/lib/`: errors (user floor)
   - `packages/server/lib/plugins/child/`: errors (user floor)
   - `packages/server/lib/`: passes (default floor)
   - `cli/test/`: passes (default floor)
3. To confirm the build order, run `rm -rf packages/network/{cjs,esm} packages/https-proxy/{cjs,esm}`, then `npx lerna run build --stream --concurrency=4`. It should pass.
4. `yarn check-ts`, `yarn health-check`, `yarn check-lockfile` and `yarn check-lockfile-drift` all pass.

Verified locally on Node 24.22.1: all of the above, plus the `@cypress/webpack-dev-server` unit tests (39 passed) and `packages/server` `test/unit/browsers/{utils,webkit}.spec.ts` (15 passed).

### How has the user experience changed?

No change. This is lint configuration and dependency declarations only; the only source edits are comments.

### PR Tasks

- [na] Is there an associated issue with maintainer approval for PR submission? Internal lint tooling, no user-facing behavior.
- [na] Have tests been added/updated? The lint run itself is the check, and the floors and build order were verified as described in Steps to test.
- [na] Has a PR for user-facing changes been opened in [`cypress-documentation`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation)?
- [na] Have API changes been updated in the [`type definitions`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/types/cypress.d.ts)?

comment.body:
`cypress/flake` reports 15 flaky tests on 41d467d. This PR doesn't cause them. Every CircleCI job passed, and each flaky test passed on retry.

- 8 of them fail on purpose to exercise retries: `runner.cy.ts › getSnapshotPropsForLog › is retried once` and `retries_test_isolation_off.cy.ts › does not navigate to about:blank between retries`, each in Chrome, Chrome Beta, Electron and Firefox.
- The other 7 are driver network, cookie and file timeouts (`intercepting_request`, `network_handling`, `cookie_misc`, `files.cy.ts`) and reporter UI timeouts (`header.cy.ts`, `reporter-ct-webpack.errors.cy.ts`). This PR changes no runtime code, only ESLint configs, `package.json` declarations and comments, so it can't affect them.
- `develop` shows the same baseline: recent full Cloud runs report 17, 16 and 12 flaky tests (runs 75305, 75302, 75298).

There's no fix to port into this PR, and the status is a Cloud report rather than a job, so there's nothing to re-run.

---

issue.title: chore: adopt eslint-plugin-n for Node runtime floors and dependencies
issue.body:
- Closes N/A. This is one slice of adopting lint plugins that enforce rules the repo already documents but checks by hand (the runtime floors in AGENTS.md "Runtime targets").

### Additional details

Adds `nodeConfig` to `@packages/eslint-config`, built on `eslint-plugin-n` ^18.5, and opts every Node-side workspace into it. It enables:

- `n/no-unsupported-features/node-builtins`, `es-builtins` and `es-syntax`
- `n/no-extraneous-import` and `n/no-extraneous-require`

**Floors.** The floors are set explicitly rather than read from `engines`, which most workspaces don't declare. Both are read at load time from the files that own them, so they can't drift:

- **Default floor:** `>=` the `.node-version` version (24.22.1). That's also the Node embedded in the pinned Electron 43.8.4, so the main process has the same floor.
- **User floor:** `userNodeConfig` lowers it to `engines.node` from `cli/package.json` (`^22.0.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0`). It applies to:
  - the shipped CLI, but not `cli/test/**`, whose specs CI runs on the dev Node
  - `packages/server/lib/plugins/child/**`, the config child process

**Opt-ins.** Every workspace opts in except the browser bundles (`app`, `launchpad`, `frontend-shared`, `driver`, `reporter`, `runner`, `extension`, `example`) and the `npm/` mount adapters. Some opted-in packages also ship browser code, and those files are left out too:

- `vite-dev-server`'s and `vite-plugin-cypress-esm`'s `client/**`
- `webpack-dev-server`'s `src/browser.ts` and `src/aut-runner.ts`

`system-tests` leaves out `projects/**` and `project-fixtures/**`, where `no-extraneous-import` crashes resolving the fixtures' tsconfig files.

**Two things the initial probe missed:**

- **Undeclared deps hidden by an unbuilt tree.** `no-extraneous-*` skips imports it can't resolve, and workspaces whose `main` points at build output don't resolve until built. Linting a built tree, as CI does, turned up 17 more hits beyond the probe's 40.
- **Node globals.** The plugin only checks globals such as `process` and `Buffer` that resolve in scope. Workspaces that never declared Node globals (`cli`, for one) were silently skipping those checks, so `nodeConfig` now declares `globals.node`.

**What the rules reported, and the fixes:**

- **Undeclared sibling workspaces:** declared as `0.0.0-development` `devDependencies`, as the repo already does, unless the declaration would close a dependency cycle. nx breaks a cycle by dropping one of its edges, which can build a package before one it compiles against. Declaring `@packages/https-proxy` in `network` did exactly that in CI (`https-proxy` built before `network`). Ten imports would close a cycle, so they aren't declared. The importing files get `undeclaredWorkspaceImports(files, workspaces)` instead, a new export that sets `allowModules` for just those files. No edge this PR adds closes a cycle.
- **Undeclared packages in `scripts`:** declared in its `dependencies`, reusing ranges already in the lockfile so nothing resolves a new copy.
- **Type-only imports:** declared `@angular-devkit/core` in `webpack-dev-server` and `@types/request` in `@packages/ts`.
- **Intentional cross-package resolution:** `eslint-disable-next-line` with a reason for `playwright-core` (found through `playwright-webkit`), `html-webpack-plugin` (found in the user's project) and the batteries-included preprocessor (found in the Cypress binary).
- **The 5 `node-builtins` hits:** 4 were the browser's `Storage` type in `cli/types/cypress.d.ts`, and 1 was `zlib.crc32` in a CLI spec that runs on the dev Node. The version rules are now off for `.d.ts` files, which emit no code.

**Notes:**

- The plugin is loaded with `require`: its types use a string-named export (`"module.exports"`) that TypeScript only parses from 5.6, and the repo is on 5.4.5.
- `n/no-process-exit` stays off, because its hits are CLIs and scripts that exit on purpose. `n/no-deprecated-api` is left for a separate slice.
- `yarn dedupe-lockfile` bumped `ignore`, `get-tsconfig` and `@eslint-community/regexpp` within their existing ranges.

`packages/eslint-config/AGENTS.md` documents the block: what it checks, the floors, which workspaces opt in and why the rest don't, the cycle rule, and the gotchas above.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Lint and dependency-declaration only; no runtime behavior changes beyond ESLint enforcement in CI and local dev.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`nodeConfig`** to `@packages/eslint-config` on **`eslint-plugin-n`**, enforcing Node/ES feature floors and **`n/no-extraneous-import` / `require`** across Node-side workspaces. Floors come from **`.node-version`** (bundled/dev) and **`cli/package.json` `engines.node`** via **`userNodeConfig`** for shipped CLI code and **`packages/server/lib/plugins/child/**`**.
> 
> Opt-in is wired through dozens of **`eslint.config.ts`** files, with **ignores** for browser bundles, webpack/vite client code, and **system-tests** fixtures. **`undeclaredWorkspaceImports`** whitelists sibling workspace imports that would create **nx build cycles** if declared in **`package.json`**.
> 
> Dependency and **`package.json`** updates (plus a few targeted **`eslint-disable`** comments) fix new extraneous-import hits; **`AGENTS.md`** documents adoption, floors, and gotchas (built tree for resolution, **`globals.node`**, **`require`** for the plugin).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 41d467d934f3d432f9514d5d2309ab18edc8a20b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

### Steps to test

1. Run `yarn build`, then `yarn lint`. It should pass. Run it on a built tree, or the dependency rules can't see workspaces whose `main` points at build output.
2. To confirm the floors fire, add `export const fs = process.getBuiltinModule('fs')` (added in Node 22.3) to a file in each place below, then run `npx eslint <file>` from that workspace:
   - `cli/lib/`: errors (user floor)
   - `packages/server/lib/plugins/child/`: errors (user floor)
   - `packages/server/lib/`: passes (default floor)
   - `cli/test/`: passes (default floor)
3. To confirm the build order, run `rm -rf packages/network/{cjs,esm} packages/https-proxy/{cjs,esm}`, then `npx lerna run build --stream --concurrency=4`. It should pass.
4. `yarn check-ts`, `yarn health-check`, `yarn check-lockfile` and `yarn check-lockfile-drift` all pass.

Verified locally on Node 24.22.1: all of the above, plus the `@cypress/webpack-dev-server` unit tests (39 passed) and `packages/server` `test/unit/browsers/{utils,webkit}.spec.ts` (15 passed).

### How has the user experience changed?

No change. This is lint configuration and dependency declarations only; the only source edits are comments.

### PR Tasks

- [na] Is there an associated issue with maintainer approval for PR submission? Internal lint tooling, no user-facing behavior.
- [na] Have tests been added/updated? The lint run itself is the check, and the floors and build order were verified as described in Steps to test.
- [na] Has a PR for user-facing changes been opened in [`cypress-documentation`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation)?
- [na] Have API changes been updated in the [`type definitions`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/types/cypress.d.ts)?

comment.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+import fs from 'fs'
+import path from 'path'
+import type { ESLint, Linter } from 'eslint'
+import globals from 'globals'
+
+// The plugin's types export a string-named `"module.exports"`, which the
+// repo's TypeScript and import-x's parser can't read, so load it untyped
+const n: ESLint.Plugin = require('eslint-plugin-n')
+
+const repoRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../..')
+
+// ESLint loads configs synchronously, so the floors can't be read async
+// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax
+const readRepoFile = (file: string) => fs.readFileSync(path.join(repoRoot, file), 'utf8')
+
+/**
+ * The Node that dev tooling and the bundled app run on. Electron's embedded
+ * Node is the bundled app's runtime, and it is no lower than `.node-version`
+ * for the Electron pinned in the root `package.json`; lower this to Electron's
+ * Node if a bump ever leaves it behind.
+ */
+const bundledNodeVersion = `>=${readRepoFile('.node-version').trim()}`
+
+/** The user's Node, which runs the `cypress` CLI and the config child process */
+const userNodeVersion: string = JSON.parse(readRepoFile('cli/package.json')).engines.node
+
+/**
+ * Opt-in Node checks for Node-side workspaces: no runtime APIs or syntax
+ * above the floor, and no imports of packages the workspace doesn't declare.
+ * Spread it after `baseConfig`. The floor is `bundledNodeVersion`; spread
+ * `userNodeConfig` after it, scoped with `files`, for code that runs on the
+ * user's Node.
+ */
+export const nodeConfig: Linter.Config[] = [
+  {
+    files: ['**/*.{js,cjs,mjs,jsx,ts,cts,mts,tsx}'],
+    plugins: {
+      n,
+    },
+    languageOptions: {
+      // The plugin only checks globals such as `process` and `Buffer` that
+      // resolve in scope
+      globals: globals.node,
+    },
comment.body:
Confirmed and fixed in 41d467d. `vite-dev-server/client/**` and `vite-plugin-cypress-esm/client/**` are browser scripts, and with `globals.node` applied, `no-undef` would no longer catch a stray `require`, `Buffer` or `__dirname` in them. `webpack-dev-server`'s `src/browser.ts` and `src/aut-runner.ts` are browser entries too. All four are now in `nodeConfig`'s `ignores` for their package, so they get no Node globals and no Node floor. I checked with `--print-config`: `Buffer` is undefined and the `n/` rules are off for those files, while the Node code in the same packages keeps both. `packages/eslint-config/AGENTS.md` documents the pattern for mixed packages.

issue.title: docs: correct cy.session() against the source, add workflow examples, and recapture screenshots
issue.body:
## Summary

This reviews the `cy.session()` API page against the Cypress v16.2.1 source and fixes what didn't match. It also adds six examples for common workflows, a lifecycle diagram, and fresh screenshots from real runs, and brings the page in line with our writing guidelines. One link in the `cy.getCookie()` page changes to follow a renamed heading.

## Why

The page had drifted from how `cy.session()` behaves, and a few examples didn't run as written. I checked every behavior claim against `packages/driver/src/cy/commands/sessions/` and confirmed each one at runtime.

**Accuracy fixes**

- **What invalidates a session.** A bare `return false` from `validate` doesn't invalidate it. A `false` yield counts only when `validate` returns nothing or returns a Cypress chain.
- **Reusing an id.** The cross-spec section framed the duplicate-id error as a cross-spec issue. It now shows the error a reused `id` with a different `setup` actually produces, next to the example that defines the session once in a shared file.
- **When data is cleared.** Session data is cleared before a restore too. With test isolation off, the page after `cy.session()` depends on whether the session was created or restored.
- **Cross-domain section.** It told readers to visit the domain before calling `cy.session()`. That visit does nothing: `cy.session()` clears the page, and a relative `cy.visit()` resolves against `baseUrl`. Its example also had a syntax error and an invented domain.
- **Choosing an id.** It suggested `uuid`, but a random `id` never matches a saved session. The custom command examples put the password in the `id`, which the page warns against because the `id` shows in the Command Log.
- **Undocumented behavior, now documented:**
  - A Promise from `setup` or `validate` has a 20-second limit.
  - `cy.session()` isn't supported inside `cy.origin()`.
  - It throws in component tests.
- **Broken examples.**
  - An invalid regex.
  - `should('eq')` called on an element.
  - Selectors that matched nothing.
  - A block that redeclared `const login` four times.

**New content**

- **Six examples:**
  - Using the status `cy.session()` yields.
  - A `validate` that skips the network.
  - Caching with test isolation disabled.
  - Signing in through an identity provider with `cy.origin()`.
  - Testing logout without ending the shared session.
  - Reusing an `id` with a different `setup`.
- **A lifecycle diagram** of the create, restore, and recreate paths.
- **Recaptured screenshots.** The old ones came from the Real World App. The expanded Command Log image didn't match its caption, and the console image showed a password inside the session `id`. Every image now comes from a Cypress 16.2.1 run of a snippet on this page. The Sessions panel screenshot also appears where the page explains the globe icon and the **Clear All Sessions** button.

**Writing guidelines**

- **Examples show the recommended way.** The custom command, helper function, and returns-a-value sections showed Before and After versions, the `cy.visit()` section opened with the pattern to avoid, and the id section had an Incorrect Usage example. Each now shows only the recommended version.
- **JavaScript and TypeScript.** The two custom command examples are `copyTsToJs` blocks, which render as JavaScript and TypeScript tabs now that #7071 is merged.
- **Formatting and wording.**
  - The options table is alphabetized.
  - The text uses present tense and active voice.
  - Bold appears only on real UI controls.
- **Headings.** They now carry their own context and use sentence case.
- **Links.** Test isolation links go to the dedicated page, and See also was refreshed.
- **Less repetition.** The `setup` argument links to the Notes section on clearing instead of repeating it.

## Notes for reviewers

- **How the examples were verified.** Every added or rewritten example ran verbatim in the `.example-check/` harness, with an assertion for each claim in the prose. Examples on stand-in hosts ran against local servers mapped to `app.cypress.io` and `auth.cypress.io`. The TypeScript blocks typecheck. Blocks whose only change was to code comments, and the id examples that call an undefined `loginWith()` for illustration, were parse-checked instead of run.
- **Screenshot capture.** The screenshots follow `scripts/screenshots/README.md` on Cypress 16.2.1. The `validate` in the Command Log snippet uses `failOnStatusCode: false`, so a failure reads as one assertion rather than a full request dump. The page explains this.
- **The diagram** passes WCAG 2.2 AA:

  | Element | Ratio |
  | --- | --- |
  | Text | 5.71:1 to 16.51:1 |
  | Lines and shapes | 3.90:1 or better |

  It simplifies one edge case: a saved session whose `setup` source changed takes the create path. That mostly matters on reruns in `cypress open`.
- **Example order.** The examples stay at H3, so they appear in the table of contents. They're ordered so related ones sit together. I tried grouping them under H3 headings, but that dropped them out of the table of contents, so I reverted it.
- **Left as is:**
  - The "E2E only" badge, which is correct. The `cypress/react` mount adapter makes `cy.session()` throw in component tests.
  - The `Chainable<void>` typing on the example custom commands.
- **CI.** The first E2E run failed one Support Assistant test that this PR doesn't touch. It passes on `main` and passed on re-run. Details are in the comment below. Later E2E "failures" on intermediate commits were runs cancelled by the next push.
- **Follow-up in `cypress-io/cypress`.** The invalid-option error says "Available options are: `validate`" but leaves out `cacheAcrossSpecs` (`packages/driver/src/cypress/error_messages.ts`). That fix belongs in the Cypress repo.

No issue is linked: this came from a direct request to review the page.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01WUv8r2DMN6bq2T9oJujuqi

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation and static assets only; no runtime or test code changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR **realigns the `cy.session()` API docs with Cypress v16.2.1 behavior** and expands guidance for common auth patterns.
> 
> **Accuracy and behavior clarifications** include when `validate` invalidates a session (e.g. bare `return false` does not), duplicate `id` rules within a spec (function source comparison), when page and session data are cleared on create vs restore, and constraints such as E2E-only usage, no `cy.session()` inside `cy.origin()`, and a 20s Promise limit for `setup`/`validate`. Examples are rewritten or fixed (ids without passwords, regex, selectors) and **six new workflow examples** cover status yields, offline validation, test isolation off, `cacheAcrossSpecs`, logout without polluting shared sessions, SSO via `cy.origin()`, and cross-domain restore.
> 
> A new **`session-lifecycle-diagram.svg`** illustrates create/restore/recreate paths; Command Log screenshots and captions are refreshed. **`cy.getCookie()`** now links to the renamed validate section anchor.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b26c5e3e3c181c2de3461a23b4525a18e477debe. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

comment.body:
**About the E2E failure in the Cypress Cloud summary above.** The first run failed one test, `cypress/e2e/support_assistant.cy.ts`: "Support Assistant > when the embed cannot load > does not show once the embed loads". It timed out waiting for a `cypressgpt:focus` message from the embed stub on all three attempts.

It isn't caused by this PR:
- The spec visits `/app/get-started/why-cypress` and tests the Support Assistant widget. This PR changes only the `cy.session()` page, its images, and one link in `cy.getCookie()`.
- The same spec passed on `main` at the commit this PR merges into (adadf4e, #7069).
- A single re-run of the failed shard passed (E2E 7/8, attempt 2). All checks on b26c5e3 are now green.

So this is an intermittent failure in that spec, not something this diff introduced. No fix for it exists yet, and it doesn't belong in this PR.
